Overview

The Arrow OverJet SP-800M brings coating, drying and Memjet DuraCore™ digital printing together on one sheet-fed line, so converters and in-house packaging teams can print cartons, corrugated board and display pieces on demand, without printing plates.

Coat, Dry and Print in One Line: Packaging boards are rarely an ideal inkjet surface. Each sheet passes through a precision coating stage and an efficient drying stage before it reaches the print engine, so the ink lands on a smooth, print-ready surface. You get stronger color and more consistent results without scheduling a separate offline priming step.

Precision Engineering: A dual CMYK printhead configuration prints at up to 1600 × 1600 dpi, with 1600 × 954 and 1600 × 640 dpi modes also available. A vacuum conveyor holds each sheet flat, the media centering guide keeps it aligned, and a mark sensor keeps every print in register, so fine text, barcodes and gradients come out clean.

Built for Packaging Production: Run sheets up to 800 mm (31.5″) wide with a 638 mm (25.1″) print width at belt speeds up to 195 ft/min. Ink is supplied from 10 L tanks, and the machine runs on three-phase 220V power. Short-run cartons, seasonal displays, pharmaceutical packaging and promotional signage can all be printed in-house, on your own schedule.

Bring packaging and display work in-house with the Arrow OverJet SP-800M. Print bigger, print better and print faster.

Memjet Technology

Memjet DuraCore™ Print Engine: The SP-800M is built on Memjet DuraCore™, Memjet’s production print engine platform that delivers its hallmark 1600 dpi quality in four-color CMYK. Paired with a dual printhead configuration, it gives the SP-800M the detail and color accuracy that premium packaging and retail display work demand.

Water-Based Pigment Inks: A high-durability, water-based pigmented aqueous ink platform delivers vibrant CMYK color on cartons, corrugated and display board, supplied from 10 L tanks for steady production.

Frequently Asked Questions

What materials can the Arrow OverJet SP-800M print on?

The SP-800M prints on duplex board and packaging materials, including cartons, corrugated board, folding boxes and foam board. It accepts sheets up to 800 mm wide with a maximum printing width of 638 mm. To confirm results on a specific board, request a sample print on your own material.

Why does the SP-800M coat the substrate before printing?

Packaging boards often absorb ink unevenly. The integrated precision coating stage applies an even, print-ready layer, and the drying stage prepares it before printing. The result is stronger color vibrancy and more consistent output, without a separate offline priming step.

What print engine powers the OverJet SP-800M?

The SP-800M is built on the Memjet DuraCore™ print engine with a dual CMYK printhead configuration. Its printheads are updated with Memjet Setanta technology, a nozzle-control system that gives finer control over print modes, keeps idle nozzles at print-ready temperature and runs faster automatic declogging cycles.

How fast does it print, and at what resolution?

The SP-800M runs at belt speeds up to 195 ft/min (59.4 m/min). It offers three resolution modes: 1600 × 1600 dpi, 1600 × 954 dpi and 1600 × 640 dpi. The Arrow team can recommend the right mode for your artwork and substrate.

What ink does the SP-800M use?

It uses a high-durability, water-based pigmented aqueous ink platform in CMYK, supplied from 10 L tanks.

What power does the SP-800M need?

The SP-800M requires three-phase 220V power (220V + N + G). Contact Arrow Systems for full site requirements, including footprint, before installation.

Can I see a sample on my own packaging material?

Yes. Send your artwork and the board stock you run today, and Arrow Systems will arrange a sample print so you can evaluate color, detail and finish on your own materials before you buy.

Arrow Lam 380

380 mm Reel-to-Reel Thermal Laminating Machine for Printed PET Films, Labels, Catalogues & Print Finishing

The Arrow Lam 380 is a compact reel-to-reel thermal laminating machine designed for consistent lamination of printed roll-fed and sheet-based print applications. Built with a heavy-duty structure, hydraulic nip pressure system, precision-controlled heated roller, and AC frequency-controlled drive, the machine delivers reliable bonding and smooth finish quality for demanding print and packaging workflows.

With a maximum lamination width of 380 mm / 15 inches, the Arrow Lam 380 is especially suitable for printed PET films, labels, catalogues, photo albums, book wrappers, and other commercial print finishing applications requiring gloss, matte, silky matte, or velvet thermal lamination.

The machine is designed as a practical, durable, and efficient thermal lamination solution for printers, label manufacturers, packaging converters, and print finishing units looking for strong film adhesion, stable operation, and long-term production reliability.

Overview
Features
Specifications
Applications
Overview

In print and packaging, lamination plays an important role in improving surface appearance, durability, handling resistance, and product presentation. The Arrow Lam 380 applies a thermal film layer over printed substrates to enhance finish quality while protecting the printed surface.

Its reel-to-reel configuration supports continuous production, making it suitable for roll-fed print and packaging applications. The machine combines hydraulic pressure, controlled heating, and manual operator adjustments to achieve reliable lamination results across different job types.

Features

Continuous Reel-to-Reel Lamination

The Arrow Lam 380 supports reel-to-reel thermal lamination, making it suitable for continuous roll-fed production and reducing manual handling during longer print finishing runs.

Hydraulic Nip Pressure

The hydraulic nip pressure system helps ensure strong bonding between the thermal film and substrate. It supports uniform pressure application for improved lamination quality and consistent results.

Precision Heated Roller Control

The heated roller is designed for controlled thermal film activation. Heat is precisely managed using an imported slip ring system, helping maintain stable lamination quality during production.

Imported AC Frequency-Controlled Drive

The machine uses an imported AC frequency-controlled variable speed drive from Control Techniques, UK, allowing operators to adjust machine speed according to the material, film type, and job requirement.

Manual Operator Control

The Arrow Lam 380 is a basic, operator-controlled model. Web tension, film tension, and nip pressure are manually adjusted, giving operators direct control over the lamination process.

Compact, Rigid & Sturdy Construction

With a compact footprint and approximate machine weight of 750 kg, the Arrow Lam 380 is built for industrial durability, stable operation, and long-term use in production environments.

Efficient Power Consumption

The machine is engineered for efficient operation with a total power consumption of approximately 4.5 kW, making it a practical choice for print and packaging units seeking reliable thermal lamination with controlled energy usage.

Print labels and flexible packaging on demand — in full colour with white — on a single compact platform that fits where you work.

White toner support makes it possible to produce clean, vivid output on clear and coloured media, including kraft labels and transparent flexible packaging film, where ink-only printing would result in washed-out or unreadable results. ANY-PRESS — Details & Specifications

The ANY-PRESS is built around a single question: what does a modern in-house label and packaging press actually need to do? The answer this machine provides covers print quality, media flexibility, colour capability, and output format — all on a platform that fits in a standard office space without specialist infrastructure.

At its core is an LED laser toner engine printing at 1,200×1,200 dpi across a 324mm working width, with five colour stations — cyan, magenta, yellow, black, and white. The white toner station is central to what the ANY-PRESS can produce: it enables opaque backgrounds and crisp text on transparent, kraft, and coloured media types that would be unusable on a four-colour-only press.

The toner print engine operates at low temperature, which broadens the range of compatible substrates beyond what heat-sensitive media would allow. It works on uncoated art paper, certified PET, and PP without requiring expensive coated label stock — directly reducing material costs per label. The LED laser process also produces output with strong environmental resistance: finished prints demonstrate high water, UV, and scratch resistance without additional coating in most applications.

On the output side, the ANY-PRESS handles both conventional roll-label production and flexible packaging in a single integrated platform. Flexible packaging formats include lay-flat pouches, stand-up pouches, and sachets across a range of sizes. An optional built-in laminator — available in cold or hot configuration — allows labels and pouches to be coated inline immediately after printing, consolidating what is otherwise a two-machine, two-pass process into a single continuous run.

Operation is straightforward. The Arrow Software RIP system handles colour management, variable data output — barcodes, QR codes, sequential numbering — and print job control. No specialist print technician is required: the machine is designed so that production staff can be trained and running in a short period. Power requirements are within standard single-phase electrical supply.

The machine does not require specially coated materials, making it compatible with art paper, kraft, PET, and PP. This helps lower material costs and gives users more flexibility in choosing media.

An integrated cold or hot laminator can be used inline after printing, streamlining the finishing process. This removes the need for a separate lamination machine and reduces extra handling.

Printed output is resistant to water, UV, and abrasion in most typical use cases. In many applications, no additional coating is needed, making it suitable for refrigerated and outdoor use.

The system supports variable data printing, including barcodes, QR codes, numbering, and personalization. All of this can be produced in a single pass without stopping production.

ANY-PRESS is designed for in-house production setups that need a practical digital label solution. With efficient consumables and low media cost, it helps keep the cost per label competitive.

The machine fits into standard office or production spaces and runs on single-phase power (110–240V). It does not require special ventilation or specialist infrastructure.

9 — No Specialist Operators Required
The system is easy to operate and requires minimal training. Teams can get started quickly without depending on expert technicians for everyday operation.

10 — High-Capacity Consumables for Lower Running Costs
High-capacity toner and drums reduce the frequency of replacements and help lower ongoing operating costs. This makes the machine more efficient for regular production use.

The output stays clean on uncoated and eco-friendly materials, avoiding the smearing issues often associated with liquid ink. It is a strong fit for kraft and sustainable packaging applications.

The ANY-CUT III also supports optional Auto Job Changeover (AJC), which reads job barcodes and transitions between different cutting configurations automatically, keeping multi-job production runs moving without operator intervention. Overview

ANY-CUT III Anytron Laser Finisher — Details & Specifications

The ANY-CUT III brings production-class laser finishing to label producers who need consistent high throughput alongside the cost and flexibility advantages of a die-free system. Running at up to 45 m/min with a 350mm web width, it produces up to 15,000 labels per hour — eliminating the bottleneck that finishing often creates in high-output digital label operations.

Like the rest of the any-CUT range, the ANY-CUT III operates without physical cutting tooling. Label geometries are defined digitally and executed directly by the laser, meaning there are no die orders to place, no tooling lead times to manage, and no changeover downtime when moving between different label shapes or job types. The transition from one job to the next happens at the software level — and with the optional Auto Job Changeover feature, it happens automatically.

The ANY-CUT III is equally well suited to short-run and long-run label production. For short runs, the absence of tooling costs makes each job economically viable regardless of volume — there is no minimum order threshold imposed by die amortisation. For long runs, the 45 m/min cutting speed and dual laser power options (150W and 250W) ensure that output rates remain competitive with conventional finishing equipment.

Material versatility is another defining capability of the ANY-CUT III. Beyond the standard paper, PET, and PP substrates common to most laser finishing systems, it also processes cardboard and reflective materials — broadening the range of label products and packaging formats that can be finished on a single machine. Long labels are handled via split cut for unlimited length capability within the 300mm cutting width.

An in-line web guide maintains media tracking accuracy to within .02mm across the full web width, and the integrated vision system ensures registration precision is maintained throughout extended production runs. The touch screen display and software interface are designed for fast operator onboarding — full training is achievable in a short period without specialist technical knowledge.

Features

1 — Up to 15,000 Labels per Hour, No Retooling

The ANY-CUT III processes up to 15,000 labels per hour at a maximum cutting speed of 45 m/min. Unlike conventional die-cutting equipment, it achieves this output without requiring tooling setup between jobs. There is no time lost to die installation, no minimum run length to make a job tooling-viable, and no retooling cost when the label shape changes. The laser is always ready for the next job.

2 — 350 mm Web Width

With a maximum web width of 350mm (13.8 inches) and a cutting area of 300mm, the ANY-CUT III handles label media widths that sit above the compact and mid-tier finishing class. An unwinder roll diameter of up to Ø700mm and a rewinder of up to Ø400mm are supported, allowing large-format roll stock to be processed without intermediate rewinding.

3 — Two Laser Power Configurations: 150W and 250W

The ANY-CUT III is available with either a 150W or 250W CO2 water-cooled laser. The 150W configuration handles standard label substrates across the full range of paper, film, and synthetic materials. The 250W option provides additional cutting power for thicker substrates, higher-speed production, or applications where deeper laser penetration is required. Both configurations operate with a laser spot size of 260 µm.

4 — Fast Turnaround: No Die-Related Delays

Conventional finishing requires physical dies to be ordered, delivered, installed, tested, and replaced when worn. For the ANY-CUT III, none of this applies. Label shapes are defined in software and loaded as job files. The time between receiving a new label design and starting production is measured in minutes, not days. description:
Filtrabox Expand

Expand 1 Fume Extractor

The Expand 1 is a powerful fume extractor that can be used for a number of industries including printing, health and beauty supplies, laser cutting, laser engraving, and many more. It uses a unique filtration system that has three stages:

The Pre-filter

In this stage, and particles that has been extracted with the fumes will be taken up by this first filter. Utilizing the pre-filter allows us to achieve longer life in the HEPA and Carbon filters by keeping them clean of debris. Our unique cylindrical shape allows for more surface area for the particles to attach to before the filter has to be replaced.

The HEPA Filter

The HEPA Filter, or High Efficiency Particle Air Filter, filters out the smaller particles that may have passed through the Pre-filter undetected. These smaller particles are trapped in the HEPA filter while the rest of the fumes get pushed into the final stage.

The Carbon Filter

The final stage of the filtration process is passing the fumes through a bed of activated carbon. The carbon filter removes all remaining contaminant and impurities in the fumes before recirculating the clean air back into the environment.
